subproblems.title: Dilation change of variables for H^n set integrals over blow-up images η_{x,r}(M)
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^N (= Euclidean N) and r > 0. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be an arbitrary set and F : ℝ^N → ℝ an arbitrary function. Let η := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x), and let H^n := μHE[n]. Then ∫_{η(M)} F dH^n = r⁻¹^n · ∫_M F(η(z)) dH^n(z), as Bochner set integrals. No measurability or integrability of M or F is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (x : Euclidean N) (r : ℝ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (F : Euclidean N → ℝ), 0 < r → ∫ y in Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, F y ∂μHE[n] = r⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z in M, F (Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)), the change of variables (∗), here for arbitrary M and F. Provenance (orientation only): the same argument was accepted on another DAG branch for an identically typed lemma named frt_wat_setIntegral_blowUpMap_image. That declaration is not available on this branch and its name is reserved there. Do not reference it; prove this child under its own name exactly as below. The proof is self-contained.

Notation: H := μHE[n]; η := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η(y) = r⁻¹ • (y − x) (the definition unfolds by rfl); ψ(y) := x + r • y. All integrals are Bochner integrals, and nothing is assumed about M or F.

1. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^N with inverse ψ. Since r ≠ 0, ψ(η(y)) = x + r • (r⁻¹ • (y − x)) = x + (y − x) = y and η(ψ(y)) = r⁻¹ • ((x + r • y) − x) = r⁻¹ • (r • y) = y. Both maps are continuous, being built from translations and scalings. Hence η is a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding) and is injective. In Lean one may take η := (Homeomorph.subRight x).trans (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹ (inv_ne_zero hr.ne')), whose underlying function is Chapter03.blowUpMap x r by rfl.

2. Scaling of H under η⁻¹. Let S ⊆ ℝ^N be any set, not necessarily measurable. Since ψ inverts η, η⁻¹(S) = ψ(S) = τ(r • S), where τ(y) := x + y and r • S := {r • s : s ∈ S}. τ is an isometry (isometry_add_left), so H(τ(r • S)) = H(r • S) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Since r ≠ 0, H(r • S) = ‖r‖₊^n • H(S) (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). As r > 0, the [0, ∞]-valued factor ‖r‖₊^n equals ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) (enorm_eq_nnnorm, Real.enorm_eq_ofReal, ENNReal.ofReal_pow). Therefore H(η⁻¹(S)) = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) · H(S).

3. Pushforward of H. For every Borel S, (H.map η)(S) = H(η⁻¹(S)) (Measure.map_apply; η is continuous, hence measurable). By step 2 this equals ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) · H(S) = (ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H)(S). By Measure.ext, H.map η = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H.

4. Pushforward of H⌞M. Since η is a measurable embedding, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map gives (H.map η).restrict(η(M)) = (H.restrict(η⁻¹(η(M)))).map η, and η⁻¹(η(M)) = M by injectivity (Set.preimage_image_eq). Combining this with step 3 and Measure.restrict_smul:
 (H.restrict M).map η = (H.map η).restrict(η(M)) = (ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H).restrict(η(M)) = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H.restrict(η(M)).

5. Change of variables. Because η is a measurable embedding, ∫ G d(ν.map η) = ∫ G(η(z)) dν(z) for every measure ν and every function G : ℝ^N → ℝ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map; G need not be measurable). Take ν := H.restrict M and G := F. Then use step 4 and integral_smul_measure (∫ G d(c • ν') = c.toReal · ∫ G dν'):
 ∫_M F(η(z)) dH(z) = ∫ F d((H.restrict M).map η) = (ENNReal.ofReal(r^n)).toReal · ∫_{η(M)} F dH = r^n · ∫_{η(M)} F dH.
 The last step is ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, using r^n ≥ 0.

6. Since r⁻¹^n · r^n = (r⁻¹ · r)^n = 1, multiplying the identity of step 5 by r⁻¹^n gives r⁻¹^n · ∫_M F(η(z)) dH(z) = ∫_{η(M)} F dH. Here η(M) = Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M and F(η(z)) = F (Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z), so this is exactly the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: η = blowUpMap x r is a homeomorphism with inverse y ↦ x + r • y, hence an injective measurable embedding.
For every set S, H^n(η⁻¹ S) = H^n(x + r • S) = r^n H^n(S) (translation isometry and Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀).
H^n.map η = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H^n (Measure.ext on Borel sets).
(H^n⌞M).map η = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H^n⌞η(M) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, η⁻¹(η M) = M, Measure.restrict_smul).
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure give ∫_M F∘η dH^n = r^n ∫_{η(M)} F dH^n; multiply by r⁻¹^n.

subproblems.title: H^n of a closed disc in an n-dimensional subspace: H^n(P ∩ B̄_r(0)) = ω_n r^n
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let P be a linear subspace of ℝ^N = Euclidean N with dim P = n (Module.finrank ℝ P = n), and let r ∈ ℝ with r ≥ 0. Then μHE[n](P ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n, i.e. H^n(P ∩ B̄_r(0)) = ω_n r^n. Here H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N, and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Euclidean N)) (r : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n → 0 ≤ r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ((P : Set (Euclidean N)) ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal r ^ n
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)), the plane-ball measure H^n(P ∩ B̄_s(0)) = ω_n s^n, stated directly for a subspace P with finrank P = n. Provenance (orientation only): the same argument, for P = T.plane with T ∈ G(N, n), was accepted on another DAG branch for a lemma named intcpt_canon_plane_closedBall_hausdorff. That declaration is not available on this branch. Do not reference it; prove this child under its own name exactly as below. Stating the lemma for a Submodule removes the Grassmannian.ofSubmodule detour. The proof is self-contained.

Notation: P is viewed as a real inner product space with the restricted inner product and the subspace (Borel) σ-algebra; hP : finrank ℝ P = n; ι : P → ℝ^N is the inclusion (Subtype.val).

1. P ∩ closedBall 0 r = ι(closedBall (0 : P) r). Indeed, z lies in the left side iff z ∈ P and ‖z‖ ≤ r, iff z = ι(w) for some w ∈ P with ‖w‖ = ‖z‖ ≤ r. Prove it by ext, using ⟨z, hz⟩ for one inclusion and w.2 for the other.

2. ι is an isometry (isometry_subtype_coe). Isometries preserve the Euclidean Hausdorff measure of images (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), so μHE[n](ι(closedBall (0:P) r)) = μHE[n]_P(closedBall (0:P) r), where μHE[n]_P is μHE[n] on the metric space P.

3. On every finite-dimensional real inner product space E, μHE[finrank E] = volume (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Taking E = P and rewriting finrank ℝ P = n inside this equation gives μHE[n]_P = volume_P.

4. volume_P is an additive Haar measure on P. So for r ≥ 0, volume_P(closedBall (0:P) r) = ofReal(r^(finrank P)) · volume_P(ball (0:P) 1) = ofReal(r^n) · volume_P(ball (0:P) 1) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall, then hP). This also holds for n = 0 and for r = 0.

5. Let e : P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) be the coordinate map of an orthonormal basis of P indexed by Fin n, e.g. ((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ P).reindex (finCongr hP)).repr. A linear isometry equivalence between finite-dimensional inner product spaces preserves volume (LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving). Also e⁻¹(ball 0 1) = ball (0:P) 1, because ‖e w‖ = ‖w‖. Since balls are measurable (measurableSet_ball), MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage gives volume_P(ball (0:P) 1) = volume(ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) = unitBallVolume n (the definition of unitBallVolume).

6. Combining steps 1–5 with ofReal(r^n) = ofReal(r)^n for r ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pow): μHE[n](P ∩ closedBall 0 r) = ofReal(r)^n · unitBallVolume n = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n (mul_comm). ∎ (For n = 0, P = {0} and both sides equal 1, consistent with the general argument.)

Lean route (checked in a scratch copy after import GMT.Ch08.Submission; axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound): prove the set identity of step 1 by ext; obtain hvol : (μHE[n] : Measure P) = volume from InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume (V := P) by rwa [hP]; rw [himage, isometry_subtype_coe.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, hvol, Measure.addHaar_closedBall volume (0 : P) hr, hP]; prove volume (ball (0:P) 1) = unitBallVolume n with e.measurePreserving.measure_preimage measurableSet_ball.nullMeasurableSet after ext/simp for the preimage; finish with ENNReal.ofReal_pow hr and mul_comm.
proof_key_steps: P ∩ B̄_r(0) is the image of the closed r-ball of the n-dimensional inner product space P under the isometric inclusion.
Isometry invariance of μHE[n] and μHE[finrank P] = volume_P.
Haar scaling: volume_P(B̄_r(0)) = ofReal(r^n) · volume_P(ball 0 1).
A linear isometry P ≃ ℝ^n carries volume_P(ball 0 1) to ω_n = unitBallVolume n; ofReal(r^n) = ofReal(r)^n.

subproblems.title: Two-sided eventual ball-mass bounds ⇒ Θ^n(μ, x) = a
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on Euclidean N, x ∈ Euclidean N and a ∈ [0, ∞]; write ω_n = unitBallVolume n. Assume (i) for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < a · ω_n, eventually as t → 0⁺, c · ENNReal.ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(closedBall x t); and (ii) for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with a · ω_n < c, eventually as t → 0⁺, μ(closedBall x t) ≤ c · ENNReal.ofReal(t)^n. Then HasDensity n μ x a, i.e. μ(B̄_t(x))/(ω_n t^n) → a as t ↓ 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (x : Euclidean N) (a : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, c < a * unitBallVolume n → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n ≤ μ (closedBall x t)) → (∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, a * unitBallVolume n < c → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μ (closedBall x t) ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n) → HasDensity n μ x a
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)), the final squeeze, carried out directly in [0, ∞]. Provenance (orientation only): the same argument was accepted on another DAG branch for an identically typed lemma named frt_td_hasDensity_of_ball_mass_bounds. That declaration is not available on this branch and its name is reserved there. Do not reference it; prove this child under its own name exactly as below. The proof is self-contained.

Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1); B_t(x) := closedBall x t. By definition, densityRatio n μ x t = μ(B_t(x)) / (ω · ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n), and HasDensity n μ x a means Tendsto (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 a).

Hypotheses:
(H₋) for every c < a · ω, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(B_t(x));
(H₊) for every c > a · ω, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, μ(B_t(x)) ≤ c · ofReal(t)^n.

1. 0 < ω < ∞. The open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is nonempty and open, and volume there is an additive Haar measure, hence positive on nonempty open sets: ω > 0 (measure_ball_pos volume 0 one_pos). The ball is bounded in a proper space, so ω < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). (For n = 0 the space is a point, the ball is the whole space and ω = 1.)

2. The normalizer. For t > 0 put D_t := ω · ofReal(t)^n.
 - D_t ≠ 0: ofReal(t) > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos), so ofReal(t)^n ≠ 0, and ω ≠ 0.
 - D_t ≠ ∞: ω ≠ ∞ and ofReal(t)^n ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.pow_ne_top, ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top).
 By definition densityRatio n μ x t = μ(B_t(x)) / D_t.

3. Reduction. [0, ∞] carries the order topology, so by tendsto_order it suffices to show:
 (a) for every b < a, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, b < densityRatio n μ x t;
 (b) for every b > a, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, densityRatio n μ x t < b.

4. Proof of (a). Let b < a. Since [0, ∞] is densely ordered, pick b' with b < b' < a (exists_between). By step 1, multiplication by ω is strictly monotone (ENNReal.mul_lt_mul_left with ω ≠ 0, ω ≠ ∞), so c := b' · ω < a · ω. By (H₋), ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(B_t(x)). Also ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, t > 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). For such t, by associativity, b' · D_t = (b' · ω) · ofReal(t)^n = c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(B_t(x)). Hence b' ≤ μ(B_t(x)) / D_t by ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le, using D_t ≠ 0 and D_t ≠ ∞ from step 2. Therefore b < b' ≤ densityRatio n μ x t.

5. Proof of (b). Let b > a. Pick b' with a < b' < b (exists_between). As in step 4, c := b' · ω > a · ω. By (H₊), ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, μ(B_t(x)) ≤ c · ofReal(t)^n = b' · (ω · ofReal(t)^n). ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul (no side conditions) then gives μ(B_t(x)) / (ω · ofReal(t)^n) ≤ b', i.e. densityRatio n μ x t ≤ b' < b.

6. Conclusion. Steps 3–5 give Tendsto (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 a), which is HasDensity n μ x a. If a = ∞ then (b) is vacuous, and if a = 0 then (a) is vacuous, so the argument covers every a ∈ [0, ∞]. ∎
proof_key_steps: 0 < ω < ∞; for t > 0 the normalizer ω·ofReal(t)^n lies in (0,∞).
tendsto_order reduces the claim to: eventually b < ratio for every b < a, and eventually ratio < b for every b > a.
For b < a pick b < b' < a; apply the lower hypothesis with c = b'ω < aω and use ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le.
For b > a pick a < b' < b; apply the upper hypothesis with c = b'ω > aω and use ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul.

subproblems.title: Cutoff sandwich: ν(B̄_{ra}(x)) ≤ ofReal(r^n ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x+ry) dH^n) ≤ ν(B̄_{rR}(x))
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be H^n-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ ≥ 0 on M, x ∈ ℝ^N and r₀ ∈ ℝ with θ H^n-integrable on M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x). Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 everywhere, f(y) = 1 whenever ‖y‖ ≤ a and f(y) = 0 whenever ‖y‖ > R (a, R ∈ ℝ). Let r > 0 with r·R ≤ r₀. Put ν := (H^n⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ), η := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r (η(z) = r⁻¹(z − x)) and I := ∫_{η(M)} f(y)·θ(x + r•y) dH^n(y). Then ν(B̄_{r·a}(x)) ≤ ofReal(r^n · I) ≤ ν(B̄_{r·R}(x)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (x : Euclidean N) (f : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ)) (r₀ a R r : ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 ≤ θ y) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall x r₀) μHE[n] → (∀ y, 0 ≤ f y) → (∀ y, f y ≤ 1) → (∀ y, ‖y‖ ≤ a → f y = 1) → (∀ y, R < ‖y‖ → f y = 0) → 0 < r → r * R ≤ r₀ → (((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict M).withDensity fun y ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (θ y)) (closedBall x (r * a)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n * ∫ y in Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, f y * θ (x + r • y) ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n * ∫ y in Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, f y * θ (x + r • y) ∂μHE[n]) ≤ (((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict M).withDensity fun y ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (θ y)) (closedBall x (r * R))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 (cutoff comparison and sandwich) of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)), for one cutoff f and one radius r. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; B̄_s(z) := closedBall z s; ν := (H^n⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ); η := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, η(z) = r⁻¹ • (z − x); I := ∫_{η(M)} f(y) θ(x + r•y) dH^n(y); and
 J := ∫⁻_M ofReal(f(η z)) · ofReal(θ z) dH^n(z) ∈ [0, ∞].

1. Where f ∘ η is 0 or 1. For every z, ‖η z‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖ = dist(z, x)/r (norm_smul, norm_inv, r > 0, dist_eq_norm).
 - If z ∈ B̄_{ra}(x), then dist(z, x) ≤ r·a, so ‖η z‖ ≤ a and f(η z) = 1.
 - If z ∉ B̄_{rR}(x), then dist(z, x) > r·R, so ‖η z‖ > R and f(η z) = 0.

2. ν on closed balls. For every s ∈ ℝ the closed ball B̄_s(x) is Borel, so
 ν(B̄_s(x)) = ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ofReal θ d(H^n⌞M) (withDensity_apply)
 = ∫⁻_M 1_{B̄_s(x)}(z) · ofReal θ(z) dH^n(z) (lintegral_indicator).
 Neither step needs measurability of θ.

3. Sandwich of J. For every z:
 1_{B̄_{ra}(x)}(z) · ofReal θ(z) ≤ ofReal(f(η z)) · ofReal θ(z) ≤ 1_{B̄_{rR}(x)}(z) · ofReal θ(z).
 - Left inequality: for z ∈ B̄_{ra}(x), f(η z) = 1 by step 1 and both sides are equal; otherwise the left side is 0.
 - Right inequality: for z ∈ B̄_{rR}(x), ofReal(f(η z)) ≤ 1 because f ≤ 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_le_one); otherwise f(η z) = 0 by step 1 and the middle term is 0.
 Integrating over H^n⌞M (lintegral_mono, which needs no measurability) and using step 2 gives ν(B̄_{ra}(x)) ≤ J ≤ ν(B̄_{rR}(x)).

4. J < ∞. Since r·R ≤ r₀, B̄_{rR}(x) ⊆ B̄_{r₀}(x), so by step 3 and monotonicity J ≤ ν(B̄_{r₀}(x)). Moreover
 ν(B̄_{r₀}(x)) = ∫⁻_{B̄_{r₀}(x)} ofReal θ d(H^n⌞M) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)} ofReal θ dH^n (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, inter_comm),
 which is finite because θ is H^n-integrable on M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x) (Integrable.lintegral_lt_top).

5. Change of variables. Apply the sibling lemma blowup_cov (Submission.intcpt_id_tpd_setIntegral_blowUpMap_image N n x r M F hr) to F(y) := f(y)·θ(x + r•y). It gives I = r⁻¹^n ∫_M f(η z) θ(x + r•η z) dH^n(z). Since x + r•η(z) = x + r•(r⁻¹•(z − x)) = z (smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀, one_smul, add_sub_cancel), this is I = r⁻¹^n ∫_M g dH^n with g(z) := f(η z)·θ(z). Hence r^n · I = ∫_M g dH^n, because r^n · r⁻¹^n = (r · r⁻¹)^n = 1.

6. Bochner integral as a lintegral: ∫_M g dH^n = J.toReal. Apply integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae for the measure H^n⌞M; it needs (a) and (b).
 (a) g ≥ 0 H^n⌞M-a.e.: M is H^n-null-measurable, so H^n⌞M-a.e. z lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀). There θ(z) ≥ 0, and f ≥ 0 everywhere.
 (b) g is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M. Let B := B̄_{r₀}(x), a closed (hence measurable) set. By step 1 and B̄_{rR}(x) ⊆ B, g vanishes off B, so g = 1_B · g. By aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff it suffices that g is AEStronglyMeasurable for (H^n⌞M)⌞B = H^n⌞(B ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). The function z ↦ f(η z) is continuous (f continuous, η affine), hence AEStronglyMeasurable for every measure. θ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞(M ∩ B), being integrable on M ∩ B = B ∩ M. So the product g is AEStronglyMeasurable there.
 The lemma gives ∫_M g dH^n = (∫⁻_M ofReal(g z) dH^n).toReal. Since f(η z) ≥ 0, ofReal(g z) = ofReal(f(η z)) · ofReal(θ z) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, lintegral_congr). Hence the lintegral is J.

7. Conclusion. By steps 5–6, r^n · I = J.toReal, so ofReal(r^n · I) = ofReal(J.toReal) = J (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, J ≠ ∞ by step 4). Step 3 now reads ν(B̄_{ra}(x)) ≤ ofReal(r^n · I) ≤ ν(B̄_{rR}(x)). ∎
proof_key_steps: ‖η z‖ = dist(z,x)/r, so f∘η = 1 on B̄_{ra}(x) and f∘η = 0 off B̄_{rR}(x).
ν(B̄_s(x)) = ∫⁻_M 1_{B̄_s(x)} ofReal θ dH^n (withDensity_apply, lintegral_indicator); pointwise comparison and lintegral_mono give ν(B̄_{ra}) ≤ J ≤ ν(B̄_{rR}).
J ≤ ν(B̄_{r₀}(x)) = ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_{r₀}(x)} ofReal θ dH^n < ∞ by integrability of θ.
Change of variables (sibling blowup_cov) with x + r•η(z) = z: r^n·I = ∫_M f(η z)θ(z) dH^n.
That integrand is a.e. ≥ 0 (ae_restrict_mem₀) and AEStronglyMeasurable (indicator of B̄_{r₀}(x)), so the integral equals J.toReal; then ofReal(r^n I) = J.

subproblems.title: Radial cutoff f ∈ C_c with 1_{B̄_a} ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_R} and ω_n a^n ≤ ∫_P f dH^n ≤ ω_n R^n
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, P a linear subspace of ℝ^N = Euclidean N with dim P = n, and a, R ∈ ℝ with 0 < a < R. Write H^n := μHE[n] and ω_n := (unitBallVolume n).toReal. Then there is f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) such that: 0 ≤ f ≤ 1; f(y) = 1 whenever ‖y‖ ≤ a; f(y) = 0 whenever ‖y‖ > R; and ω_n a^n ≤ ∫_P f dH^n ≤ ω_n R^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Euclidean N)) (a R : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n → 0 < a → a < R → ∃ f : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), (∀ y, 0 ≤ f y) ∧ (∀ y, f y ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ y, ‖y‖ ≤ a → f y = 1) ∧ (∀ y, R < ‖y‖ → f y = 0) ∧ (unitBallVolume n).toReal * a ^ n ≤ ∫ y in (P : Set (Euclidean N)), f y ∂μHE[n] ∧ ∫ y in (P : Set (Euclidean N)), f y ∂μHE[n] ≤ (unitBallVolume n).toReal * R ^ n
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 4 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)): the cutoff functions and their integrals over the tangent plane. With (a, R) = (κ, 1) the cutoff below is the selected proof's f₁, and with (a, R) = (1, κ⁻¹) it is f₂. Notation: H^n := μHE[n] on E := Euclidean N; B̄_s := closedBall (0 : E) s; ω̂ := unitBallVolume n ∈ [0, ∞]; ω_n := ω̂.toReal; hP : finrank P = n; 0 < a < R.

1. The cutoff. Let g(y) := min{1, max{0, (R − ‖y‖)/(R − a)}}, where R − a > 0.
 - g is continuous: it is built from the norm, affine maps, max and min (fun_prop).
 - 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 everywhere.
 - If ‖y‖ ≤ a, then (R − ‖y‖)/(R − a) ≥ 1, so g(y) = 1.
 - If ‖y‖ ≥ R, then (R − ‖y‖)/(R − a) ≤ 0, so g(y) = 0. In particular g(y) = 0 whenever ‖y‖ > R.
 So g vanishes outside B̄_R, which is compact (isCompact_closedBall; E is proper), and g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro). Let f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) be g packaged with these proofs (⟨⟨g, continuity⟩, compact support⟩). Then f(y) = g(y) for all y, and f has the four pointwise properties.

2. Plane balls. For s ≥ 0, H^n(P ∩ B̄_s) = ω̂ · ofReal(s)^n by the sibling plane_ball (Submission.intcpt_id_tpd_plane_closedBall_hausdorff N n P s hP hs). Also ω̂ < ∞, as ω̂ is the volume of a bounded ball in a proper space (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence:
 - (H^n⌞P)(B̄_s) = H^n(B̄_s ∩ P) = ω̂ · ofReal(s)^n < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply, inter_comm; finiteness by ENNReal.mul_ne_top, using ω̂ ≠ ∞ and ofReal(s)^n ≠ ∞ from ENNReal.pow_ne_top and ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top);
 - the indicator 1_{B̄_s} : E → ℝ is H^n⌞P-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const);
 - ∫_P 1_{B̄_s} dH^n = (H^n⌞P).real(B̄_s) = (ω̂ · ofReal(s)^n).toReal = ω_n · s^n (integral_indicator_one, measureReal_def, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal).
 In Lean, type the indicator explicitly as (closedBall 0 s).indicator (1 : E → ℝ).

3. Integrability of f on P. f is continuous, hence AEStronglyMeasurable. Also |f| ≤ 1_{B̄_R} pointwise: on B̄_R, |f| = f ≤ 1; off B̄_R, f = 0. The bound is H^n⌞P-integrable by step 2 with s = R ≥ 0, so f is H^n⌞P-integrable (Integrable.mono').

4. Comparison. Pointwise 1_{B̄_a} ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_R}:
 - on B̄_a, f = 1; elsewhere the left side is 0 ≤ f;
 - on B̄_R, f ≤ 1; elsewhere f = 0.
 Integrate over P (integral_mono, with the integrability from steps 2–3) and use step 2 with s = a and s = R (both ≥ 0). This gives ω_n a^n ≤ ∫_P f dH^n ≤ ω_n R^n. ∎
proof_key_steps: Explicit cutoff g(y) = min{1, max{0, (R − ‖y‖)/(R − a)}}: continuous, [0,1]-valued, 1 on B̄_a, 0 off B̄_R, compact support; package as f ∈ C_c.
Sibling plane_ball: H^n(P ∩ B̄_s) = ω̂ ofReal(s)^n < ∞, so 1_{B̄_s} is H^n⌞P-integrable with ∫_P 1_{B̄_s} = ω_n s^n.
|f| ≤ 1_{B̄_R}, so f is H^n⌞P-integrable.
integral_mono on 1_{B̄_a} ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_R} gives ω_n a^n ≤ ∫_P f ≤ ω_n R^n.

subproblems.title: Lower ball-mass bound at a weighted approximate tangent point
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be H^n-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ ≥ 0 on M, x ∈ ℝ^N, P a linear subspace of ℝ^N, and r₀ > 0 with θ H^n-integrable on M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x). Assume M has weighted approximate tangent space P at x with respect to θ (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P: dim P = n and ∫_{η_{x,t}(M)} f(y)θ(x + t y) dH^n(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dH^n as t ↓ 0 for all f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ)). Let ν := (H^n⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ) and ω̂_n := unitBallVolume n. Then for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < ofReal(θ(x)) · ω̂_n, eventually as t → 0⁺: c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ ν(B̄_t(x)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (x : Euclidean N) (P : Submodule ℝ (Euclidean N)) (r₀ : ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 ≤ θ y) → 0 < r₀ → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall x r₀) μHE[n] → Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P → ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, c < ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) * unitBallVolume n → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n ≤ (((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict M).withDensity fun y ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (θ y)) (closedBall x t)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–5 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)), lower half: the inner cutoff f₁ (1_{B̄_κ} ≤ f₁ ≤ 1_{B̄_1}) and the liminf bound, written for a single c. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; B̄_s(z) := closedBall z s; ν := (H^n⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ); ω̂ := unitBallVolume n; ω := ω̂.toReal; η_t := Chapter03.blowUpMap x t; and, for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), I_f(t) := ∫_{η_t(M)} f(y) θ(x + t•y) dH^n(y). The hypothesis HWATS gives finrank P = n (first component) and, for each f, I_f(t) → θ(x) ∫_P f dH^n along 𝓝[>] 0 (second component).

0. 0 < ω̂ < ∞. ω̂ is the volume of the open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Volume is an additive Haar measure, hence positive on the nonempty open ball (measure_ball_pos volume 0 one_pos), and the ball is bounded in a proper space (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence ω = ω̂.toReal > 0 (ENNReal.toReal_pos) and ω̂ = ofReal ω. (For n = 0 the space is a point and ω̂ = 1.)

1. Fix c with c < ofReal(θ(x)) · ω̂.
 - θ(x) > 0: otherwise ofReal(θ(x)) = 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_of_nonpos), the right side is 0, and c < 0 is impossible in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.not_lt_zero).
 - So ofReal(θ(x)) · ω̂ = ofReal(θ(x)·ω) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). In particular c < ∞.
 - Put c' := c.toReal ≥ 0, so c = ofReal(c'). Then c' < θ(x)·ω (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff, as θ(x)·ω > 0).

2. Choice of κ. The map κ ↦ θ(x)·ω·κ^n is continuous at κ = 1 with value θ(x)·ω > c'. So eventually along 𝓝[<] 1 it exceeds c' (Filter.Tendsto.eventually_const_lt). Also Ioo 0 1 ∈ 𝓝[<] 1 (Ioo_mem_nhdsLT). The filter 𝓝[<] 1 on ℝ is non-trivial (1 is a limit of points below it), so the intersection of these two eventual sets is nonempty (Filter.Eventually.and, Filter.Eventually.exists). Pick κ in it: 0 < κ < 1 and c' < θ(x)·ω·κ^n. (For n = 0 any κ ∈ (0,1) works.)

3. Inner cutoff. Apply the sibling plane_cutoff (Submission.intcpt_id_tpd_plane_cutoff) to P with (a, R) := (κ, 1), using finrank P = n and 0 < κ < 1. It gives f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) with: 0 ≤ f ≤ 1; f(y) = 1 for ‖y‖ ≤ κ; f(y) = 0 for ‖y‖ > 1; and ω·κ^n ≤ ∫_P f dH^n.

4. Limit. By HWATS applied to f, I_f(t) → θ(x)·∫_P f dH^n as t ↓ 0. Moreover
 c' < θ(x)·ω·κ^n = θ(x)·(ω·κ^n) ≤ θ(x)·∫_P f dH^n (θ(x) > 0, step 3).
 Hence ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, c' < I_f(t) (Filter.Tendsto.eventually_const_lt).

5. Sandwich. Also ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, t ∈ (0, r₀] (Ioc_mem_nhdsGT, r₀ > 0). Fix t in both eventual sets. Apply the sibling ball_sandwich (Submission.intcpt_id_tpd_ball_sandwich) with (f, r₀, a, R, r) := (f, r₀, κ, 1, t). Its hypotheses are: M null-measurable, θ ≥ 0 on M, integrability on M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x), the four pointwise properties of f, t > 0, and t·1 ≤ r₀. Its right inequality gives ofReal(t^n · I_f(t)) ≤ ν(B̄_{t·1}(x)) = ν(B̄_t(x)).

6. Conclusion. For such t:
 c · ofReal(t)^n = ofReal(c') · ofReal(t^n) = ofReal(t^n · c') (ENNReal.ofReal_pow with t ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul with c' ≥ 0, mul_comm)
 ≤ ofReal(t^n · I_f(t)) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, since t^n ≥ 0 and c' < I_f(t))
 ≤ ν(B̄_t(x)) (step 5).
 This holds for all t in a set belonging to 𝓝[>] 0, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: 0 < ω̂ < ∞; c < ofReal(θ x)·ω̂ forces θ(x) > 0 and c = ofReal(c') with c' < θ(x)ω.
Choose κ ∈ (0,1) with c' < θ(x)ωκ^n (continuity of κ^n at 1).
Sibling plane_cutoff with (a,R) = (κ,1): f ∈ C_c, 1_{B̄_κ} ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_1}, ωκ^n ≤ ∫_P f.
HWATS: I_f(t) → θ(x)∫_P f > c', so eventually c' < I_f(t).
For 0 < t ≤ r₀, sibling ball_sandwich gives ofReal(t^n I_f(t)) ≤ ν(B̄_t(x)); hence c·ofReal(t)^n = ofReal(t^n c') ≤ ν(B̄_t(x)).

subproblems.title: Upper ball-mass bound at a weighted approximate tangent point
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be H^n-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ ≥ 0 on M, x ∈ M, P a linear subspace of ℝ^N, and r₀ > 0 with θ H^n-integrable on M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x). Assume M has weighted approximate tangent space P at x with respect to θ (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P). Let ν := (H^n⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ) and ω̂_n := unitBallVolume n. Then for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with ofReal(θ(x)) · ω̂_n < c, eventually as t → 0⁺: ν(B̄_t(x)) ≤ c · ofReal(t)^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (x : Euclidean N) (P : Submodule ℝ (Euclidean N)) (r₀ : ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 ≤ θ y) → x ∈ M → 0 < r₀ → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall x r₀) μHE[n] → Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P → ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) * unitBallVolume n < c → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), (((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict M).withDensity fun y ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (θ y)) (closedBall x t) ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–5 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)), upper half: the outer cutoff f₂ (1_{B̄_1} ≤ f₂ ≤ 1_{B̄_{1/κ}}) and the limsup bound, written for a single c. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; B̄_s(z) := closedBall z s; ν := (H^n⌞M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ); ω̂ := unitBallVolume n; ω := ω̂.toReal ≥ 0; η_t := Chapter03.blowUpMap x t; I_f(t) := ∫_{η_t(M)} f(y) θ(x + t•y) dH^n(y). HWATS gives finrank P = n and I_f(t) → θ(x)∫_P f dH^n along 𝓝[>] 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ).

0. ω̂ < ∞, since it is the volume of a bounded ball in a proper space (measure_ball_lt_top), so ω̂ = ofReal ω. Also θ(x) ≥ 0 because x ∈ M.

1. Case c = ∞. For t > 0, ofReal(t) > 0, so ofReal(t)^n ≠ 0 and ∞ · ofReal(t)^n = ∞ (ENNReal.top_mul). Then ν(B̄_t(x)) ≤ ∞ holds for every t ∈ (0, ∞), a set in 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Assume from now on c ≠ ∞.

2. Put c' := c.toReal, so c = ofReal(c'). Since θ(x) ≥ 0, ofReal(θ(x)) · ω̂ = ofReal(θ(x)·ω) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). So ofReal(θ(x)·ω) < ofReal(c'), which gives θ(x)·ω < c' (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff').

3. Choice of κ. κ ↦ θ(x)·ω·(κ⁻¹)^n is continuous at κ = 1, because inversion is continuous at 1 ≠ 0. Its value there is θ(x)·ω < c', so eventually along 𝓝[<] 1 it stays below c' (Filter.Tendsto.eventually_lt_const). Intersect with Ioo 0 1 ∈ 𝓝[<] 1 (Ioo_mem_nhdsLT). The filter 𝓝[<] 1 on ℝ is non-trivial, so the intersection is nonempty (Filter.Eventually.and, Filter.Eventually.exists). Pick κ in it: 0 < κ < 1 and θ(x)·ω·(κ⁻¹)^n < c'. Then κ⁻¹ > 1 (one_lt_inv₀).

4. Outer cutoff. Apply the sibling plane_cutoff (Submission.intcpt_id_tpd_plane_cutoff) to P with (a, R) := (1, κ⁻¹), using finrank P = n and 0 < 1 < κ⁻¹. It gives f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) with: 0 ≤ f ≤ 1; f(y) = 1 for ‖y‖ ≤ 1; f(y) = 0 for ‖y‖ > κ⁻¹; and ∫_P f dH^n ≤ ω·(κ⁻¹)^n.

5. Limit. By HWATS applied to f, I_f(t) → θ(x)·∫_P f dH^n. Moreover
 θ(x)·∫_P f dH^n ≤ θ(x)·(ω·(κ⁻¹)^n) = θ(x)·ω·(κ⁻¹)^n < c' (θ(x) ≥ 0, step 4).
 Hence ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, I_f(t) < c' (Filter.Tendsto.eventually_lt_const).
